CFBD Punting Endpoint Overview

Source: R/cfbd_punting.R
cfbd_punting.Rd

  • cfbd_punting_players_season(): Get player season punting and punt return production.

  • cfbd_punting_players_games(): Get player game punting and punt return production.

  • cfbd_punting_teams_season(): Get team season punting production, kicking and receiving.

  • cfbd_punting_teams_games(): Get team game punting production, kicking and receiving.

  • cfbd_punting_plays(): Get individual punt plays with yardage, field position and outcome.

Details

Get player season punting production

  cfbd_punting_players_season(year = 2025, team = "Texas")

Get player game punting production

  cfbd_punting_players_games(year = 2025, week = 5)

Get team season punting production

  cfbd_punting_teams_season(year = 2025, team = "Texas")

Get team game punting production

  cfbd_punting_teams_games(year = 2025, week = 5)

Get individual punt plays

  cfbd_punting_plays(year = 2025, week = 1, team = "Texas")

The player punting and return blocks

The two player endpoints carry a 15-column punting block, prefixed punting_ (e.g. punting_net_yards_per_punt), and a 10-column punt return block, prefixed returning_. A player who only punted has NA return columns, and the reverse.

The punting block:

col_nametypedescription
puntsintegerPunts.
punt_yards_availableintegerPunts with known gross yards (the denominator for yards_per_punt).
punt_yardsintegerGross punt yards over those punts.
yards_per_puntdoubleGross yards per punt.
longest_puntintegerLongest punt, in gross yards.
punts50plusintegerPunts of 50 or more gross yards.
net_punt_yards_availableintegerPunts with known net yards (the denominator for net_yards_per_punt).
net_punt_yardsintegerNet punt yards over those punts: gross yards minus return yards, less 20 for a touchback.
net_yards_per_puntdoubleNet yards per punt.
touchbacksintegerPunts that ended in a touchback.
fair_catchesintegerPunts fair caught.
out_of_boundsintegerPunts that went out of bounds.
downedintegerPunts downed by the kicking team.
inside20integerPunts after which the receiving team took possession inside its own 20, excluding touchbacks.
blockedintegerPunts blocked.

The return block:

col_nametypedescription
returnsintegerPunt returns.
return_yards_availableintegerReturns with known yards (the denominator for yards_per_return).
return_yardsintegerReturn yards over those returns.
yards_per_returndoubleYards per return.
longest_returnintegerLongest return, in yards.
returns20plusintegerReturns of 20 or more yards.
return_touchdownsintegerReturns for a touchdown.
fair_catchesintegerFair catches made.
muffsintegerMuffed punts.
blocksintegerPunts blocked by the player.

The team punting block

The two team endpoints carry one 24-column block twice: punting_* covers the team's own punts (so punting_return_yards is what opponents returned against it) and returning_* covers the punts it received (so returning_punts counts opponent punts and returning_return_yards is the team's own return yardage). In a game frame, one side's punting_* row matches its opponent's returning_* row.

The block is the first 15 columns of the player punting block above, then:

col_nametypedescription
returnsintegerPunt returns.
return_yards_availableintegerReturns with known yards (the denominator for yards_per_return).
return_yardsintegerReturn yards over those returns.
yards_per_returndoubleYards per return.
longest_returnintegerLongest return, in yards.
returns20plusintegerReturns of 20 or more yards.
return_touchdownsintegerReturns for a touchdown.
muffsintegerMuffed punts.
receiving_team_turnoversintegerPunts on which the receiving team lost possession, such as on a muff or fumble.

The *_available counts are denominators, not statistics. CFBD parses these fields out of play text, so a punt can be counted while its yardage stays unknown. Dividing by punts or returns instead of the matching *_available column understates every mean.

Season coverage

Unlike the passing and rushing families, these endpoints reach back to 2015. Earlier seasons answer HTTP 200 with an empty array rather than an error, so a request for 2014 returns an empty data frame, not a failure.
